definitions.explanation: The wavering visual distortion caused by heated air rising from the ground on hot days.

examples.english: Heat shimmer rises from the summer road.

examples.japanese: {陽炎|かげろう}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{遠|とお}く⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{景色|けしき}→景色：01395_keshiki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{揺|ゆ}れて→揺れる：01161_yureru⟧⟦{見|み}える→見える：01165_mieru⟧。
examples.english: The distant scenery appears to waver due to the heat haze.

examples.japanese: ⟦{真夏|まなつ}→真夏：27793_manatsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{昼下|ひるさ}がり→昼下がり：16197_hirusagari⟧、⟦アスファルト→アスファルト：10736_asufaruto⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{上|うえ}→上：00682_ue⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{陽炎|かげろう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{揺|ゆ}らめいて⟦いた→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: In the midsummer afternoon, heat haze was shimmering above the asphalt.

notes:
The kanji combine {陽|よう} (sun) and ⟦{炎|ほのお}→炎：03724_honoo⟧ (flame), reflecting the fiery shimmer visible above hot surfaces.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {陽炎|かげろう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{立|た}つ→立つ：00758_tatsu⟧: heat haze rises
- {陽炎|かげろう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{揺|ゆ}らめく: heat haze shimmers
- {陽炎|かげろう}⟦のように→のように：30291_noyouni⟧: like a mirage (fleeting, illusory)

CULTURAL NOTE:
A traditional spring ⟦{季語|きご}→季語：09561_kigo⟧ (seasonal word) in haiku, though it is most often seen on hot summer days. Its fleeting, dreamlike quality makes it a common literary image for things that are illusory or barely there.

WATCH OUT:
かげろう is also the name of the mayfly ({蜉蝣|かげろう}), another image of the short-lived; the title of the Heian-era {蜻蛉日記|かげろうにっき} plays on the word.
